title: People’s Mañanera September 10
author: Pedro Gellert
content:
_Every day, President Claudia Sheinbaum gives a morning presidential press
conference and Mexico Solidarity Media posts English language summaries,
translated by Mexico Solidarity’s Pedro Gellert. Previous press conference
summaries are available[here](https://mexicosolidarity.com/mananera/)._

**#HonestidadYResultados: The President Tours the Country  
** President Claudia Sheinbaum resumes her tour and will visit Tamaulipas,
Veracruz, Chiapas, Oaxaca, Campeche, Yucatán, Quintana Roo, and Hidalgo. A
government that is present on the ground, accessible, and accountable.

**Fewer Bureaucratic Hurdles, More Ways to Comply  
** More than 4.1 million taxpayers will benefit from simpler and digital
paperwork procedures. For small businesses, income tax (ISR) can be paid every
three months, and there will be an option to pay the 7% tax directly.

**Zero Tax Rate: A Boost for Books and Reading  
** Books will be subject to a zero tax rate. The price for readers will not
increase, and bookstores and publishers will be able to recover the tax on
their expenses. This measure provides a greater boost to publishers,
bookstores, and access to reading.

**PISA: More Young People in Classrooms, Less Inequality  
** The OECD acknowledges that more young people, especially those from
marginalized backgrounds, are attending school. Furthermore, Mexico has a
socioeconomic gap in science that is smaller than the OECD average.

**Mexico Is No One 's Punching Bag  
**In response to Secretary of State Marco Rubio's statements, the President
urged that Mexico not be used in the U.S. election campaign and reminded him
that the United States must also combat drug use, money laundering, and arms
trafficking. “Let's respect one another; to each their own elections and their
own territory.”

**La Derecha Diario: There Are Shady Tactics in Play  
** Sheinbaum pointed out that the right-wing webpage La Derecha Diario was
created to influence elections in Latin America through fake news, smear
campaigns, and artificially amplifying the circulation of such materials on
social media. She called for transparency regarding how it operates, who funds
it, and what interests lie behind it.
